title: Functional, physical and disease-specific effects of physical activity in patients with myasthenia gravis
summary:
The aim of the study is to investigate the effectiveness of exercise in patients with myasthenia gravis. In addition, we want to determine the effect of exercise on muscle strength, quality of life, everyday functionality and fatigue levels.
   
On the one hand, the study will examine whether physical activity improves activities of daily living (tested using the MG-ADL questionnaire) and, on the other hand, whether physical activity can lead to an increase in muscle mass, muscle function, quality of life and vital capacity in patients with myasthenia gravis. In addition, it will be observed and documented whether fatigue, quality of life and the quality of life can be improved by the selected exercise programme.
This study also focuses on the development of study-based recommendations for the integration of a tailored exercise programme in the treatment of myasthenia gravis. One potential benefit would be the widespread recommendation and prescription of regular physiotherapy (and video-based apps) as a further pillar in the treatment of myasthenia gravis. The aim is also to sustainably strengthen patients' motivation for sporting activities.
Patients with myasthenia gravis are divided into three groups (circuit training, video-based training, no sport) and carry this out for 12 weeks (accompanied and in dialogue with the study team).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients capable of giving consent
- Written consent to participate - Age of ≥ 18- 85 years
- Established diagnosis of generalised MG, confirmed by a positive serological test for AChR antibodies at screening (confirmed by ELISA or cell-based assay) and one of the following:
o positive decrement in the medical history proven by repeated nerve stimulation, except for the M. orbicularis oculi; or
o history of positive anticholinesterase test (e.g. edrophonium chloride or neostigmine test); or
o improvement in myasthenic symptoms with oral acetylcholinesterase inhibitors, as assessed by the study physician
- Mild or moderate disease progression (MFGA 2-3)
- at least 3 months of stable drug therapy
- able to participate in the training programmes (eligibility is determined by the investigators, see ‘Preliminary sports medical examination’)
Exclusion criteria:
- Other neurological or muscular diseases
- Serious concomitant illnesses that restrict participation in the training programme (severe heart failure, pacemaker, etc.)
- Pregnancy
- Patients unable to give consent
